subject: Regional routing contingency & TTL workaround for US/EU/APAC impact
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: SRE Team <sre@acme-corp.com>, Julia Moss <julia.moss@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 22:05:00 +0000
Subject: [Redwood] Partial regional service disruption — immediate customer routing options

Hi Julia / Acme SRE team,

We wanted to reach out proactively: starting ~21:45 UTC we observed degraded connectivity between a subset of our serving fleet and cloud egress in three regions (us-east, eu-west, ap-southeast). This has caused increased latencies and sporadic 5xxs for some customers routing through those regional exits.

What we've done so far:
- Isolated affected host pools and shift traffic away from impacted egress nodes.
- Enabled short-term fallback to our global edge and rebalanced requests.
- Throttled low-priority background requests to preserve customer-facing throughput.

Immediate options for Acme (recommended in order):
1) Region pin: add X-Redwood-Region: "global" to force global edge routing until the network fix completes.
2) Explicit region override: Set region=us-west or region=eu-central in the request query to avoid the degraded egress nodes in the affected zones.
3) Increase client retry TTL: set Retry-After = 5s with exponential backoff to mask transient 5xx during the realignment window.

Attachment: edge-routing-checklist.pdf (small checklist with sample headers and curl examples).

We’ll follow up with a short timeline and mitigation steps within 4 hours. Please reply if you want us to flip your traffic to a preferred region on your behalf — we can do that from our side and confirm once complete.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Julia Moss <julia.moss@acme-corp.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 22:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: [Redwood] Partial regional service disruption — immediate customer routing options

Thanks Neha — we’re seeing the errors in our telemetry (spike in 502/504s around 21:50 UTC). Can you confirm whether the region pin (X-Redwood-Region: global) will route through any EU egress if our tenant is normally EU-preferring? We want to avoid cross-border data egress if possible.

Also send us the sample curl snippets — I’ll share with our SRE and product infra. If you can perform the region switch for us, that would be easiest.

-Julia
SRE Lead, Acme Corp

On Wed, 11 Mar 2026 at 22:05, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> [Redwood] Partial regional service disruption — immediate customer routing options
>
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 00:10:00 +0000
Subject: FW: Acme — need region pin + data residency question

Team — looping you in. Acme asked whether the global pin will introduce EU egress for an EU tenant. Quick notes and ask:

- Marcus: confirm which egress endpoints global -> will it ever egress through eu-west for tenants with EU residency flags? If yes, can we stage a global->non-eu variant?
- Dylan: if we do a manual traffic flip, what’s the exact set of API keys/tenant ids and the window we should use to avoid token reuse issues? See attachment incident-timeline.csv for request spike details.
- Mina: customer compensation / SLA exceptions — Acme is a priority customer. Recommend we offer one incident credit and a short postmortem call.

I’ve attached the routing checklist with sample headers. Propose we do the manual flip to eu-central for Acme’s tenant to preserve data locality, and then later fail back when upstream egress fully recovered.

-Neha

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 04:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: FW: Acme — need region pin + data residency question

Neha / all — quick technical summary:
- X-Redwood-Region: global will prefer our multi-region global edge; for an EU-residency tenant that may cause egress to leave EU depending on routing decisions. Not safe for strict residency customers.
- We have a safe manual override: region=eu-central query param or header X-Redwood-Region: eu-central, which pins both routing and egress to eu-central nodes. That preserves residency.
- Manual flip plan: we can atomically update tenant routing on our control plane for Acme. Steps:
  1) Pause low-priority queues for the tenant for 30s
  2) Set tenant routing override to eu-central
  3) Warm connections on eu-central pool for 60s, monitor 4xx/5xx
  4) Re-enable queues and observe for 10 minutes

I can run this during Acme’s maintenance window or now (we have capacity). Estimated time to completion: ~6–8 minutes. I’ll coordinate with Dylan on API key scoping.

-Marcus
Principal Engineer, Runtime

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: SRE Team <sre@acme-corp.com>, Julia Moss <julia.moss@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 13:40:00 +0000
Subject: [Redwood] Action complete — Acme tenant pinned to eu-central + post-incident follow-up

Julia / Acme SRE team —

Thanks for the quick coordination. Summary of actions taken at 2026-03-12T13:36:40Z (UTC):
- We performed an atomic routing override for tenant acme-corp-42 to eu-central.
- Warmed connections and validated request success rates; observed error rate drop from 4.8% -> 0.3% within 90s.
- No cross-border egress observed during verification window.

Next steps and follow-up:
- We attached an incident timeline and the routing checklist we used.
- We’ve opened an internal RCA and will publish a customer-facing postmortem (draft link below) by EOD tomorrow.
- Compensation: as discussed, we will apply a one-time service credit equal to 10% of March usage for impacted requests; Mina will follow up to confirm the exact credit.

Postmortem (draft): https://drive.redwood.ai/incident-2026-03-11/postmortem-v1
Status page entry: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-03-11

If you’d like us to keep the tenant pinned to eu-central until the root cause is fully cleared, confirm and we’ll keep the override in place. Otherwise we can fail back during a maintenance window and notify you in advance.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

- edge-routing-checklist.pdf (curl examples, header samples)
- incident-timeline.csv (request rates and error buckets)
